The Inciting Incident

The Trigger: Slide 14

"It wasn't a proposal. It was a dissection."

At 10:14 AM, Jameson Frost clicked the remote. The screen flickered.

Up until this moment, the meeting had been tense but professional. Frost had insulted their business model, their "lack of debt," and their touring logistics. The family had endured it all with stoic amusement.

Then Slide 14 appeared.

Frost smiled. "We call this the 'Diamond in the Rough.' You have a track called Escape Velocity. Great vocals. Catchy hook. But it's fifteen minutes long. It's unlistenable. It's un-monetizable."

He pressed a button. A speaker on the conference table crackled to life.

It played a 30-second loop. Omni-Global producers had taken Cassidy's voice, stripped away the music, and layered it over a generic car-commercial beat. They had cut Ryan's guitar solo entirely.

"We fixed it," Frost said. "We cut the fat."

Asset Optimization: IP Efficiency

Project: Golden Goose // Target: Catalog ID #95-AA

Case Study: "Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)"

Current State (Legacy)
  • Runtime: 15:33 NON-VIABLE
  • Structure: Complex "Prog" Arrangement
  • Problem: 9-minute Guitar Solo blocks vocal hook
Proposed Strategy
  • Action: Isolate Female Vocal Stems
  • Action: Delete Instrumental Bridge "Dead Weight"
  • Result: 3:30 Radio Edit + SUV Sync License

Projected Uplift: +400% ROI

The Meltdown

"They are going to rip my baby apart!"

Cassidy O'Connell didn't see a slide. She saw a knife. Escape Velocity (Ad Astra) wasn't a product; it was the autobiography of her trauma. She wrote the notes. She wrote the lyrics. She directed her family. It was the safe space Ryan had built for her with his guitar.

She began to hyperventilate. It was a Level 5 Autistic Meltdown, triggered by the profound violation of her core identity.

Protocol: Ironhead Wall

10:19 AM: Ryan O'Connell spun his chair 180 degrees, turning his back on Jameson Frost to attend to his sister. Simultaneously, Evan and Tyler Wright stood up and stepped forward, blocking the executives' line of sight. They became a physical wall, shielding Cassidy's vulnerability from corporate eyes.

The Pivot

Holly O'Connell did not stand up. She did not look at Cassidy. She looked at Jameson Frost. And for the first time in the meeting, she smiled. It was the smile of a predator who had just decided to stop playing with its food.

Negotiation Status: TERMINATED WITH EXTREME PREJUDICE
